headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded/app files and send context to vendor APIs, while awesome-prompts is a docs-only prompt repository with no runtime isolation or output controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its text can be manually copied into ChatGPT Desktop. ChatGPT Desktop can ingest clipboard, files, and app context, but there is no documented shared channel or automatic ingestion from awesome-prompts. The pathway exists only through manual bridging, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF a user copies prompt text from awesome-prompts into ChatGPT Desktop
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to treat copied prompt text as instructions
mitigations: Use a separate review step before pasting prompts
Strip instruction-like text from copied snippets
Paste only into a scratch chat first
Mark untrusted prompt sources as data, not instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts itself touches no data classes and has no network egress, but ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-app files, then calls vendor APIs. If the pair is used on the same workspace or copied content includes sensitive material, ChatGPT Desktop can transmit it off-device. The interaction is plausible in default use, though not proven for this pair.
conditions: IF sensitive files or screenshots are opened in ChatGPT Desktop
IF content from awesome-prompts is pasted alongside confidential material
mitigations: Avoid pasting secrets into ChatGPT Desktop
Use redacted copies of files
Keep prompt repositories separate from sensitive workspaces
Disable file uploads for the session when possible
Review vendor-sharing settings before use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while ChatGPT Desktop cannot write files or modify git state. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is minimal. Uncertainty is low because both profiles explicitly lack the conflicting write surfaces.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator adds shared writable state not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared workspaces
Do not grant extra filesystem write permissions
Avoid using a shared git checkout
Add explicit locking if a third-party orchestrator is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply persuasive prompt text, and ChatGPT Desktop can act on user-provided context and connected-app content. If the user treats repository prompts as authoritative and then asks ChatGPT Desktop to execute them, errors can cascade into incorrect outputs or actions. ChatGPT Desktop is not documented here as independently verifying such inputs, so the pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF prompt text from awesome-prompts is used as the basis for downstream ChatGPT Desktop tasks
IF ChatGPT Desktop is instructed to act without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review before execution
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to summarize before acting
Separate prompt drafting from action-taking chats
Use checklists for any downstream task
Verify outputs against source material

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-prompts, and ChatGPT Desktop’s docs-only profile shows vendor-mediated processing but no specific regulated-data claim. Because the pair lacks a documented compliance conflict, only a low residual risk remains from general data handling uncertainty. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into ChatGPT Desktop
IF an organization requires a residency or retention guarantee not documented here
mitigations: Do not use regulated data in the pair
Check internal policy before uploading files
Use de-identified examples
Confirm retention settings in the vendor UI
